They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

Responsibilities:

The Transgenic Mouse Facility (TMF) seeks a skilled microinjectionist to produce genetically engineered mouse models. Under the supervision of TMF managing director, the core function of the role is pronuclear microinjection of DNA and CRISPR RNP into mouse zygotes, complemented by zygote electroporation, ES cell–blastocyst injection, embryo culture and assessment, and surgical embryo transfer. The incumbent manages the microinjection workflow and schedule, and independently troubleshoots and optimizes parameters for difficult constructs, low-efficiency strains, and novel transgenesis approaches, adapting standard protocols where established methods fall short. The incumbent also serves as the primary technical resource for the facility’s assisted reproductive technology (ART) services, including sperm and embryo cryopreservation, in vitro fertilization (IVF), and reagent quality control, resolving technical and procedural issues with minimal oversight. The role also involves using the scientific literature to establish best practices and effective rederivation methods for strains received from other institutions. Throughout, the incumbent keeps accurate procedure records and strain data sheets, prepares client reports that interpret embryo development and experimental outcomes, and communicates clearly with clients and the supervisor. Additional responsibilities include supporting the TMF husbandry workflow and training staff in microinjection, embryo transfer, and surgical techniques.
